posts.title: Boston’s Deadly Molasses Flood: The Warnings Nobody Acted On
posts.content:
On January 15, 1919, roughly 2.3 million gallons of molasses swept through Boston’s North End. Twenty-one people died. This evidence-based documentary investigates the leaking tank, the industrial disaster, the rescue and the negligence findings that followed.

Research: City of Boston, Massachusetts historical records, and Smithsonian Magazine. Archival images and labelled reconstructions are credited in the production package.

Subscribe to Facts Uncovered: Stories & Evidence for carefully researched history.

posts.title: Scientists Read a Roman Scroll Without Opening It — What Was Inside?
posts.content:
Buried by Vesuvius in AD 79, Herculaneum's fragile papyrus scrolls resisted reading for nearly 2,000 years. In 2026, researchers digitally unwrapped the surviving portion of PHerc. 1667 using X-ray imaging and computational reconstruction. We examine how it works and why PHerc. 172 and PHerc. 139 are separate discoveries.

Sources: Vesuvius Challenge, University of Kentucky and Diamond Light Source. Illustrated reconstructions are labelled and context images are credited.

Subscribe to Facts Uncovered: Stories & Evidence for history grounded in evidence.

posts.title: Three Ancient Scrolls, Three Different Discoveries #Shorts
posts.content:
PHerc. 1667, PHerc. 172 and PHerc. 139 made different contributions to Herculaneum research. They are three separate manuscripts, not one scroll.
